jobs.title: Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture - Corporate Technology Services
jobs.description:
Accelerate your success at Colliers.

Why Colliers?

As one of Canada’s leading commercial real estate services firms, we are driven by our mission to accelerate success for our people, clients, and communities.

A career at Colliers gives you the opportunity to make an impact, advance your career, and collaborate with top-tier talent. Don’t just take our word for it – we’ve been recognized as a top employer on a number of prestigious lists, including Best Workplaces in Canada, Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams, among others.

Toronto, ON / Vancouver, BC, Hybrid

About The Role

As Global Domain Enterprise Architect, Corporate Technology Systems within our Global Enterprise Architecture organization, you’ll define the global architectural direction for the technology platforms supporting Colliers’ corporate functions. You’ll partner with business and technology leaders to simplify and modernize our global technology landscape, establish scalable standards, and ensure major technology investments translate into sustainable business outcomes. Support global time zones: Work closely with stakeholders across Pacific and APAC regions, with flexibility to adjust working hours on most days as business needs require.

Lead global enterprise architecture: Define current-state, target-state, and transition architectures, roadmaps, principles, and standards across ERP, Finance, HCM, Procurement, CRM/MarTech, Legal, Risk & Compliance, ECM, and other corporate platforms.
Drive modernization and simplification: Lead application portfolio rationalization and recommend where platforms should be standardized, modernized, consolidated, replaced, or retired to reduce technical debt and complexity.
Shape strategic technology investments: Provide architecture leadership for major transformation initiatives, evaluating SaaS and enterprise platforms against business value, integration, data, security, scalability, total cost, and long-term strategic fit.
Advance AI, data, and integration strategy: Establish scalable patterns for enterprise data, APIs, integration, automation, AI, identity, and shared services while embedding security, privacy, governance, and regulatory requirements.
Collaborate across the global enterprise: Partner with senior business leaders, Product, Data & AI, Cloud & DevOps, Cybersecurity, Integration, Legal, Procurement, Risk, and strategic vendors to turn architecture strategy into executable outcomes.

What You Bring

Education: Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business, or a related discipline preferred.
12+ years of relevant experience: Significant experience in enterprise architecture, domain architecture, technology strategy, or large-scale transformation within complex global or federated organizations.
Enterprise platform architecture expertise: Demonstrated experience architecting and modernizing complex technology portfolios, including experience across at least two of the following three domains: Finance/ERP, HR/HCM, and CRM/MarTech.
Strong technical and transformation expertise: Deep understanding of SaaS platforms, application rationalization, enterprise integration, APIs, data architecture, cloud, cybersecurity, identity, AI/automation, and executable transition roadmaps.
Executive influence and communication: Proven ability to advise senior executives, challenge vendor and solution assumptions, and translate complex architectural decisions into clear business outcomes while remaining technically credible with architecture and engineering teams.

What We Offer

Innovative projects:
Work on cutting-edge initiatives that shape our communities, drive our growth, and make a tangible impact.

Career growth:
Advance your career and achieve your goals with industry-leading training and development programs.

Competitive benefits & compensation:
Enjoy a comprehensive and flexible benefits package along with competitive compensation that rewards your contributions and supports your well-being.

Collaborative culture:
Join our enterprising team where innovation thrives, collaboration is key, and our people are empowered to be their authentic selves and do their best work.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion:
Our robust North American Diversity & Inclusion Program features eight Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), where you can connect, learn, and contribute to a diverse and supportive community. Learn more: https://www.collierscanada.com/en-ca/careers/diversity-and-inclusion

Global network
: Join a global team of 28,000 professionals across 70 countries, where you'll expand your network and learn from experts in a dynamic international community. Accelerate your career and enhance your expertise as you connect and collaborate with top talent around the world.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in Canada on a full-time basis. The employer will not sponsor applicants for work visas.

Direct applicants only please, no agencies.

Colliers is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity in its workforce. Colliers encourages applications from all qualified individuals and will accommodate applicants' disability-related needs, up to the point of undue hardship, throughout all stages of the recruitment and selection process. If you require a disability-related accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please contact the recruitment team by email at careers@colliers.com.

jobs.title: Product Strategy and Operations, Director - New Verticals | Housing
jobs.description:
About EliseAI

At EliseAI, we're improving the industries that matter most: housing and healthcare. Everyone needs a place to live and access to quality healthcare, yet both are often harder to secure than they should be.

By integrating AI agents deeply into existing workflows, we make them more efficient, reduce costs, and improve the experience for everyone.

Housing: We simplify how renters tour apartments, sign leases, submit maintenance requests, and stay connected with their property team—bringing everything they need for their home into one place.
Healthcare: We make it easy to schedule appointments, complete intake forms, and we help patients communicate with providers, so everyone can focus on health instead of paperwork.

With EliseAI, organizations reduce manual work, improve accessibility, and deliver a seamless experience across essential services. We recently raised a $350 million funding round at a $4 billion valuation led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Bessemer Venture Partners to accelerate this mission.

About The Role

As Director of New Verticals, you will lead a team focused on identifying, incubating, and scaling new products and market opportunities from concept through launch (“zero to one”) and growth (“one to ten”). Reporting to the VP of New Verticals, you will set strategic direction, guide high-impact initiatives, and drive alignment across the organization. This role requires strategic thinking, strong leadership, deep market expertise, and proven success launching and scaling new products or businesses. You will play a pivotal role in shaping new product direction and go-to-market strategies.

Key Responsibilities

Product and Market Strategy:

Lead market research, feasibility analyses, and competitive assessments to identify and prioritize opportunities
Develop and own go-to-market strategies, including segmentation, positioning, pricing, and launch execution
Lead cross-functional teams across Product, Engineering, Go-To-Market (GTM), and Customer Success to ensure alignment and successful execution of product launches and expansions
Continuously monitor market trends, customer feedback, and competitive dynamics to iterate and optimize product strategies and offerings

Strategic Project Leadership

Develop and manage detailed project plans across the New Verticals team with clear timelines, milestones, resource allocation, and success metrics
Manage the New Verticals team and own accountability for outcomes, ensuring project milestones are met and strategic objectives are achieved

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Partner closely with internal stakeholders, including senior leadership, product managers, engineers, marketing, sales, and customer success teams, to ensure cohesive execution of strategic initiatives
Provide strategic insights and recommendations to senior leadership based on thorough analysis and market intelligence
Foster cross-functional communication and collaboration to enable seamless execution of strategic initiatives

Requirements

9-10+ years of experience in product strategy, corporate strategy, consulting, product management, or similar roles in technology or high-growth startups.
Proven track record launching and scaling new products or business lines, with clear strategic vision and measurable results.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, leveraging data and market insights for decision-making.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, effectively influencing diverse stakeholders.
Autonomous, proactive, and comfortable navigating ambiguity in fast-paced environments.
Relentless execution focus, delivering tangible outcomes.
Willingness to work in person at our office 4-5 days a week

Why Join

Growth and impact. It’s not often that you can get in on the ground floor of a funded startup that’s scaling. That means that instead of following a playbook, you’ll be writing it. Every single day you will be challenged to identify how we can scale and execute on it. You’ll learn what works when you succeed and what doesn’t when you fail. Either way, the rest of the team will be here to support you.

Benefits

In addition to the growth and impact you’ll have at EliseAI, we offer competitive salaries along with the following benefits:

Equity in the company in the form of stock options
Medical, Dental and Vision premiums covered at 100%
Fully paid parental leave
Commuter benefits
401k benefits
Monthly fitness stipend
A collaborative in-office environment with an open floor plan, fully stocked kitchen, and company-paid lunch
Fun company social events through our Elise and the City program
Unlimited vacation and paid holidays
We'll cover relocation packages and make the move exciting, not painful!

Job Compensation Range

The salary range for this role is $250,000 - $300,000 USD/CAD. EliseAI offers a competitive total rewards package which includes base salary, equity, and a comprehensive benefits & perks package. Exact compensation is determined based on a number of factors including experience, skill level, location and qualifications which are assessed during the interview process. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided by our Recruiting Team during the hiring process.

EliseAI provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Employment with EliseAI is on an “at-will” basis, meaning that either the employee or the company may terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause or notice, subject to applicable law.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We will also consider qualified applicants in accordance with the Austin Fair Chance Hiring Ordinance.

If you need assistance or a reasonable accommodation during the application or recruiting process due to a disability, please contact us at interview.accommodations@meetelise.com.

jobs.title: Practice Director, Microsoft Dynamics 365
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Practice Director, Microsoft Dynamics 365 based in Canada.

As the Practice Director, Microsoft Dynamics 365, you will lead the strategic development, growth, and overall performance of a major enterprise technology practice. You will take ownership of its business strategy, financial performance, revenue growth, and service delivery excellence, with a primary focus on Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (F&O) and a complementary focus on Business Central. Combining deep ERP expertise with strong commercial leadership, you will drive market expansion, develop new business opportunities, and strengthen strategic client relationships. You will also build and lead high-performing teams capable of delivering complex, enterprise-scale digital transformation projects. Working closely with Sales, Cloud, Data & AI, Integration, and Managed Services teams, you will help shape integrated technology solutions and accelerate business growth. This is an exciting opportunity to influence organizational strategy, strengthen Microsoft partnerships, and establish a leading position in the Dynamics 365 ecosystem.

Accountabilities

Define and execute the overall Dynamics 365 practice strategy, roadmap, and investment priorities, positioning Finance & Operations as the primary growth driver and Business Central as a complementary offering.
Take full ownership of the practice's financial performance, including P&L management, revenue growth, profitability, margins, utilization, budgets, and forecasts.
Develop and execute growth plans covering revenue targets, bookings, workforce capacity, hiring strategies, and investments required to scale the practice.
Lead the expansion of Dynamics 365 services, particularly across Finance, Supply Chain Management, Commerce, and Project Operations, while establishing scalable delivery capabilities for Business Central.
Drive business development and market expansion by generating new opportunities, strengthening existing client relationships, and increasing the pipeline for large-scale Dynamics 365 engagements.
Develop and implement go-to-market strategies, including target industries, sales initiatives, commercial positioning, and pursuit strategies for both F&O and Business Central.
Build and lead a dedicated sales and pre-sales organization, collaborating with Sales leadership to improve forecasting accuracy, acquisition performance, and deal conversion.
Serve as executive sponsor for strategic opportunities, leading deal shaping, commercial negotiations, and high-value client engagements.
Strengthen relationships with Microsoft, Dynamics 365 ISVs, partner organizations, and industry stakeholders to develop strategic alliances, co-selling initiatives, and joint go-to-market opportunities.
Identify and develop industry-specific solutions, implementation accelerators, and managed services to expand the practice's service portfolio and market differentiation.
Drive account expansion through upselling, cross-selling, and legacy ERP modernization and migration initiatives.
Establish delivery governance frameworks, quality standards, risk management processes, and operational best practices across all Dynamics 365 engagements.
Act as the senior escalation point for complex or critical projects, ensuring delivery excellence, effective change management, strong user adoption, and measurable business outcomes.
Build, develop, and inspire a high-performing leadership team comprising Practice Leads, Solution Architects, Functional Consultants, and Delivery Leaders.
Oversee talent acquisition, succession planning, professional development, Microsoft certifications, and employee retention initiatives.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and client-focused execution.
Collaborate with Cloud, Data & AI, Integration, and Managed Services leadership to deliver comprehensive, integrated enterprise solutions.
Represent the Dynamics 365 practice at executive level with clients, partners, and internal stakeholders, contributing to broader corporate strategy, growth initiatives, and potential M&A integration activities.

Requirements

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
At least 10 years of experience in ERP consulting or enterprise applications, including significant experience in senior leadership positions.
Extensive expertise in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, particularly Finance and Supply Chain Management, with working knowledge of Dynamics 365 Business Central.
Strong background in financial planning and analysis (FP&A), accounting, and program management, combined with hands-on experience advising customers on business planning and finance transformation.
Demonstrated success building, scaling, and managing Dynamics 365 practices, including responsibility for business growth, pipeline generation, new client acquisition, and revenue and margin performance.
Proven experience leading complex, large-scale Dynamics 365 implementations and enterprise transformation programs.
Strong financial and commercial acumen, with experience managing P&L, budgets, forecasts, profitability, and business performance.
Established relationships with Microsoft account teams and partner organizations, with practical experience in co-selling initiatives, strategic alliances, and Microsoft partner programs.
Familiarity with Dynamics 365 licensing models, product roadmaps, release cycles, industry solutions, and the broader Microsoft partner ecosystem.
Microsoft Dynamics 365 certifications, particularly in Finance or Supply Chain Management, are considered an asset.
Experience building and managing large, geographically distributed consulting and delivery organizations.
Strong executive presence and communication skills, with the ability to influence C-suite stakeholders, senior clients, technology partners, and internal leadership teams.
Excellent strategic thinking and business development capabilities, with the ability to translate long-term objectives into actionable growth initiatives.
Strong leadership and interpersonal skills, including the ability to inspire teams, build relationships, manage change, and create alignment across business functions.
Decisive, accountable, and comfortable navigating complex decisions and fast-paced, high-growth environments.
A client-centric mindset, with a strong commitment to delivering measurable business outcomes and long-term customer value.
Entrepreneurial and growth-oriented approach, with enthusiasm for building teams, scaling technology practices, and driving continuous innovation.

Benefits

Fully remote working arrangement within Canada.
Senior executive leadership opportunity with ownership of a strategic and growing Microsoft Dynamics 365 practice.
Opportunity to shape business strategy, influence market positioning, and drive significant revenue and organizational growth.
Exposure to enterprise-scale digital transformation initiatives and complex Dynamics 365 F&O and Business Central implementations.
Opportunity to develop strategic relationships with Microsoft, technology partners, and major enterprise clients.
Leadership role with the ability to build and develop high-performing teams and influence long-term organizational direction.
Opportunity to collaborate across Cloud, Data & AI, Integration, and Managed Services practices.
Professional growth through exposure to emerging Microsoft technologies, strategic partnerships, and enterprise transformation programs.

jobs.title: Director, Global Supply Strategic Portfolio
jobs.description:
Department
: Global Supply

Reports to
:
Senior Vice President, Global Supply

Location
: Portland, OR or North Vancouver, BC

Your Opportunity at ARC’TERYX:

Against the backdrop of business growth, a competitive landscape and functional transformation, the Arc’teryx Global Supply team is focused on evolving our operating model to source the most innovative outdoor products.

As the Director, Global Supply Strategic Portfolio, you will create the connective tissue across Global Supply's most important transformation and capability-building priorities. You will translate strategy into an integrated multi-year portfolio, establish clear governance, and help leaders make explicit choices about priorities, resources, dependencies, and investment. You will partner closely with leaders across Sourcing, Costing, Product Integrity, Manufacturing, Partner Management, Planning, Sustainability, Product Creation, Finance, Technology, and other enterprise functions to accelerate delivery and make progress and impact visible. You will also serve as a versatile strategic thought partner, stepping into high-priority work where additional leadership, structure, analysis, or execution capacity is needed . This is an opportunity to build a new capability, shape how Global Supply operates at scale, and establish the functional processes, data/technology roadmaps that enable sustained results.  

This role is based out of our Portland, Oregon office or our North Vancouver, BC office and is open to hybrid remote work. Candidates must be eligible to work in either the USA or Canada. Compensation will be paid in the currency of country located.

Meet Your Future Team:

The Global Supply team enables Arc'teryx to create and deliver over 20 million units and $1 Billion spend of exceptional, innovative apparel, footwear, hard goods & accessories product through a range of sourcing, costing, quality, manufacturing, partner management, planning, sustainability, and supply-chain capabilities. This role will be part of the Global Supply leadership team and establish the Strategic Portfolio, connecting the function's strategy to execution by aligning roadmaps, strengthening the operating model, and coordinating the process, data, technology, and change agenda across Global Supply and the broader enterprise.

If you were the Director, Global Supply Strategic Portfolio now, here are some of the core activities you would be doing:

Leading the integrated Global Supply strategic portfolio, partnering with functional leaders to translate strategy into coherent multi-year roadmaps, priorities, resource choices, dependencies, milestones/ success metrics, and investment decisions

Establishing portfolio governance and standards, maintaining portfolio visibility and accountability

Facilitating the design and implementation of the Global Supply operating-model with functional leaders including functional forums, accountabilities, decision rights, reporting & communications and ways of working with Product Creation, Supply Chain, People & Culture and enterprise partners

Connecting business priorities to integrated process, data, analytics, and technology roadmaps with clear outcomes, ownership, and measurable value

Providing thought partnership and hands-on project leadership to functional leaders, supplementing teams and filling critical white space across transformation initiatives

Leading cross-functional change and results reviews that embed transformation as an enduring organizational capability rather than a collection of stand-alone projects

Building, coaching, and deploying a high-performing strategic portfolio capability that combines structured problem solving, program leadership, business analysis, and executive communication

Are you our next Director of Global Supply Strategic Portfolio?

You have a bachelor's degree in business, operations, supply chain, engineering, finance, technology, or a related field; an advanced degree or recognized project/program management qualification is valued where paired with relevant experience.

You have 10+ years of progressive experience leading strategy, transformation, portfolio management, enterprise PMO, management consulting, or complex cross-functional programs in a global product, consumer, retail, or manufacturing environment.

You bring strong knowledge of global supply-chain and product creation operating models, ideally across apparel, footwear, equipment, or another technically complex consumer-products industry.

Strategy-to-results leader who turns ambition into clear roadmaps, milestones, success measures, and business outcomes.

Strategic integrator who connects priorities, resources, process, data, and technology across complex functional boundaries.

Operator and accelerator who moves seamlessly between strategy and execution to remove barriers and advance transformation.

High-influence leader who simplifies complexity, constructively challenges thinking, and creates alignment without relying on authority.

The salary range for this role for Portland, OR is USD$173,000 - USD$211,000.

The salary range for this role for North Vancouver, BC is CAD$167,000 - CAD$205,000.

Equal Opportunity

Arc’teryx is committed to actively creating and fostering a culture of inclusivity where voices are heard, people are seen, and values are respected. We care about the uniqueness of our applicants, employees, and guests, and we do so in a safe space fueled by curiosity and acceptance. 

Creating an inclusive workplace is connected to our core value Do Right while also having the added benefit of helping make our business better. We believe inclusion helps us to create a healthier, happier workplace, drive creativity and innovation, and reflect the communities where we operate.  

All applicants, employees, and guests can expect equality of opportunity and fair treatment in alignment with our values.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Chief Financial Officer (CFO) based in Canada.

As Chief Financial Officer, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the financial strategy and long-term growth of a fast-growing technology business. Reporting directly to the CEO and serving as a member of the Executive Team, you will act as a strategic partner in business planning, capital allocation, and investment decisions. You will oversee Finance, Legal, Corporate Governance, Insurance, Risk Management, and Revenue Operations Finance, ensuring the organization has the structure and financial discipline needed to scale. You will also lead board and investor relations, drive financial performance, and develop scalable operational and commercial frameworks. Combining executive leadership with hands-on financial expertise, you will build and mentor a high-performing finance function. This is an opportunity to influence strategic direction and contribute to a mission-driven technology company focused on improving education through innovation.

Accountabilities

Partner with the CEO and Executive Team to define corporate strategy, establish growth priorities, and guide financial planning and capital allocation decisions.
Lead board-level financial communications, including preparing financial presentations, developing performance narratives, and supporting board committees.
Manage investor relations, including shareholder communications, investor updates, financial data rooms, and due diligence processes.
Develop and oversee capital strategies, including fundraising initiatives, debt financing, and preparation for potential mergers and acquisitions.
Build, lead, and develop the finance function, initially managing a direct report while identifying future organizational and resource requirements.
Own the annual operating plan, workforce planning, long-range financial models, and revenue and bookings forecasts.
Oversee revenue modelling, cash flow management, liquidity, runway planning, and financial scenario analysis.
Establish and monitor SaaS financial performance metrics, including Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR), gross and net revenue retention, churn, bookings, and pipeline-to-revenue conversion.
Analyze unit economics, including Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC), customer lifetime value (LTV), payback periods, and gross margins, using cohort, churn, and expansion insights to support strategic decisions.
Deliver monthly financial and operational performance reports to the Leadership Team and comprehensive quarterly reporting to the board.
Maintain robust internal financial controls, audit readiness, revenue recognition practices, and compliance with Canadian and US tax requirements.
Define the organization's legal and contract strategy while managing external legal counsel, including service scope, relationships, and associated costs.
Establish and oversee contractual frameworks covering Master Subscription Agreements, Order Forms, Data Processing Agreements (DPAs), and partner, reseller, integration, and vendor agreements.
Review and manage complex contract negotiations, school district contract amendments, non-standard commercial terms, and RFP responses, exercising signing authority within board-approved limits.
Serve as Corporate Secretary, overseeing board and shareholder resolutions, meeting minutes, corporate records, and governance documentation.
Manage the capitalization table and equity programs, including stock option grants, vesting schedules, equity plan administration, and fair market value (FMV) and 409A valuations.
Oversee legal disputes, demand letters, and litigation matters in collaboration with external counsel.
Lead corporate insurance and risk management programs, including general liability, cyber liability, errors and omissions (E&O), directors and officers (D&O), and employment practices coverage.
Manage insurance broker relationships, policy renewals, certificates of insurance, and claims.
Collaborate with the CEO, Chief Revenue Officer (CRO), and sales leadership to develop pricing, packaging, and commercial strategies.
Establish pricing governance frameworks, including discount approval processes, non-standard contract terms, and deal desk oversight for complex district and multi-year agreements.
Design annual sales and customer experience compensation plans, quotas, and incentive documentation in collaboration with commercial leadership.
Oversee monthly sales commission processes, including calculations, approvals, clawbacks, commission splits, special performance incentives (SPIFs), and dispute resolution.

Requirements

CPA designation is mandatory.
12+ years of professional experience in finance and accounting, including at least 5 years in a senior finance leadership position such as CFO, VP of Finance, or equivalent.
Previous senior leadership experience within a SaaS business or high-growth technology company.

jobs.title: Director of Governance, Risk, and Compliance
jobs.description:
About EliseAI

At EliseAI, we're improving the industries that matter most: housing and healthcare. Everyone needs a place to live and access to quality healthcare, yet both are often harder to secure than they should be.

By integrating AI agents deeply into existing workflows, we make them more efficient, reduce costs, and improve the experience for everyone.

Housing: We simplify how renters tour apartments, sign leases, submit maintenance requests, and stay connected with their property team—bringing everything they need for their home into one place.
Healthcare: We make it easy to schedule appointments, complete intake forms, and we help patients communicate with providers, so everyone can focus on health instead of paperwork.

With EliseAI, organizations reduce manual work, improve accessibility, and deliver a seamless experience across essential services. We recently raised a $350 million funding round at a $4 billion valuation led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Bessemer Venture Partners to accelerate this mission.

About The Role

We are seeking a Director of Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) to scale our risk and compliance programs. This role will be instrumental in leading and scaling the GRC team to meet regulatory and IT audit readiness, manage third-party risk, and ensure our policies and processes align with industry standards.

You will work cross-functionally with Security Engineering, Legal, and business stakeholders to operationalize compliance efforts, support audits, and manage the GRC team to respond to customer and vendor due diligence requests. This is a high-impact role with direct influence on our ability to meet critical compliance timelines and support the operations of the business.

Key Responsibilities

Own and lead the company's GRC program, setting strategic direction across frameworks including SOC 1, SOC 2, PCI, HITRUST, and HIPAA
Serve as the primary owner of audit relationships, overseeing planning, evidence collection, documentation, and auditor communications
Define and enforce compliance roadmaps, ensuring cross-functional alignment and accountability on regulatory requirements
Attract top-tier talent to scale the GRC team, providing mentorship, setting priorities, and managing team performance
Oversee the vendor risk management program, including third-party due diligence, risk tiering, and escalation of critical findings
Lead reviews of vendor and client security questionnaires (DDQs) in partnership with Security Engineering, with final sign-off authority
Own the security and compliance policy framework — driving creation, review cycles, and organization-wide adoption
Partner with Legal and Security leadership on security-related contractual obligations, including review and negotiation of security addenda

Requirements

8+ years of experience in Governance, Risk, and Compliance, Information Security, or a related field, with at least 3 years in a leadership or program ownership role
Deep expertise across compliance frameworks including SOC1, SOC 2, PCI, HIPAA, and ISO certifications
Proven track record managing audit programs end-to-end, including direct relationships with external auditors
Experience building or scaling a GRC function, including team hiring and development
Strong understanding of vendor risk management, third-party due diligence, and risk-based decision-making
Ability to translate complex compliance and risk topics for executive and board-level audiences
Excellent cross-functional influencing skills — comfortable working with Legal, Engineering, and business leadership
Willingness to work in person at our office 4-5 days a week

Why Join

Growth and impact. It’s not often that you can get in on the ground floor of a funded startup that’s scaling so fast. That means that instead of following a playbook, you’ll be writing it. Every single day you will be challenged to identify how we can scale and execute on it. You’ll learn what works when you succeed and what doesn’t when you fail. Either way, the rest of the team will be here to support you.

Benefits

In addition to the growth and impact you’ll have at EliseAI, we offer competitive salaries along with the following benefits:

Equity in the company
Medical, Dental and Vision premiums covered at 100%
Fully paid parental leave
Commuter benefits
401k benefits
Fitness & home services stipend to cover part of your expenses so you can focus on what matters
A collaborative in-office environment with an open floor plan, fully stocked kitchen, and all meals covered in the office
Unlimited vacation and paid holidays
We'll cover relocation packages and make the move exciting, not painful!

Job Compensation Range

The salary range for this role is $200,000 - $275,000 USD/CAD. EliseAI offers a competitive total rewards package which includes base salary, equity, and a comprehensive benefits & perks package. Exact compensation is determined based on a number of factors including experience, skill level, location and qualifications which are assessed during the interview process. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided by our Recruiting Team during the hiring process.

EliseAI provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Employment with EliseAI is on an “at-will” basis, meaning that either the employee or the company may terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause or notice, subject to applicable law.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We will also consider qualified applicants in accordance with the Austin Fair Chance Hiring Ordinance.

The Global Supply team enables Arc'teryx to create and deliver over 20 million units and $1 Billion spend of exceptional, innovative apparel, footwear, hard goods & accessories product through a range of sourcing, costing, quality, manufacturing, partner management, planning, sustainability, and supply-chain capabilities. This role will be part of the Global Supply leadership team and establish the Strategic Portfolio, connecting the function's strategy to execution by aligning roadmaps, strengthening the operating model, and coordinating the process, data, technology, and change agenda across Global Supply and the broader enterprise.

Leading the integrated Global Supply strategic portfolio, partnering with functional leaders to translate strategy into coherent multi-year roadmaps, priorities, resource choices, dependencies, milestones/ success metrics, and investment decisions

Building, coaching, and deploying a high-performing strategic portfolio capability that combines structured problem solving, program leadership, business analysis, and executive communication

You have a bachelor's degree in business, operations, supply chain, engineering, finance, technology, or a related field; an advanced degree or recognized project/program management qualification is valued where paired with relevant experience.
